transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… it’s kind of hard to explain without sounding like I’m making a big deal out of paperwork, but for about a year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. I work around labs, so I know what I’m looking at—well, I’m a phlebotomist, not a doctor, but still, numbers don’t just… look one way and then suddenly the chart says everything is fine.

And everyone keeps telling me I’m wrong—doctors, my family, even people who don’t really look closely, they just say, “The numbers are fine.” But I know what I saw. The chart doesn’t match it. It’s just been wearing me down, going in circles trying to get someone to actually listen instead of brushing it off.
Do you believe for certain that someone in the clinic system is deliberately changing or withholding your dad’s lab results?

Yes. I mean… yes, I do. I know how that sounds, but I’ve been looking at this for almost a year, and the chart does not match what I saw.

People keep saying, “The numbers are fine,” like that settles it, but it doesn’t. I work around lab stuff every day, I know when something doesn’t look right. And it’s not even just about one number—well, it started that way, but then you start noticing how everyone acts like you’re bothering them just for asking. My family says I’m stressing myself out, and maybe I am, but I wouldn’t be if someone would just admit the records aren’t right or show me where the missing parts went.
Is it possible that you might be mistaken about someone in the clinic changing or withholding your dad’s lab results?

I mean… I guess anyone can be mistaken about little things, like maybe I wrote down a time wrong or misread a label when I was tired, but not this. Not the whole thing.

For the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and people keep telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family, everybody—but the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It just doesn’t. And I know people think I’m stuck on it, but if you worked around labs like I do, you’d understand why it bothers me. It’s been wearing me down because I keep trying to explain it and everyone acts like I’m making trouble instead of just looking at what’s missing.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?

I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like seeing a person in the room or hearing voices, if that’s what you mean. I mean, sometimes I notice things other people don’t notice, but that’s different—like when a form is worded weirdly or a number doesn’t match the way it should.

At work you kind of train yourself to catch little details, you know? People act like noticing details is the problem, but if nobody noticed details in a lab, everything would fall apart. So… no, I don’t think I’m hearing or seeing things. I’m just paying attention.
Do you think other people are trying to harm, deceive, or plot against you in areas of your life besides your dad’s lab results?

Not really… I mean, not in the same way. I don’t walk around thinking everyone is out to get me or something.

It’s this clinic situation with my dad’s labs. That’s the thing I can’t let go of, because for almost a year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in that system is changing something or holding parts back, and every time they tell me the numbers are fine it just makes me feel like they’re not looking at the same chart I saw. And then my family says I’m wearing myself down, which… I am, I know I am, but if someone would just show me the missing pieces instead of brushing me off, I wouldn’t have to keep chasing it.
Do you feel driven to repeatedly check the records or ask for reassurance about your dad’s lab results, even when you try not to?

Yes… I mean, I try not to call it “reassurance,” because that makes it sound like I just want someone to pat me on the head and say it’s okay. I want the actual chart to make sense.

But yeah, I check. I go back over what I have, the dates, the numbers, what was released and what wasn’t. Sometimes I’ll tell myself I’m not going to look at it that night, and then I end up opening it again because it’s like… if I can just find the one place where it doesn’t line up, then maybe they’ll stop saying I’m imagining it.

And it’s not like I enjoy doing that. I’m tired. I’ve been doing this for almost a year, trying to prove someone in that clinic system is changing something or holding parts of my dad’s results back, and everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine. My family, doctors—everybody. But the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It just doesn’t. So yes, I keep checking, because if I don’t, then it feels like I’m letting them get away with it.
Do you feel that your urge to keep checking your dad’s lab records is unreasonable or excessive?

Unreasonable… I don’t know. Excessive, maybe, if you look at how much time it takes. I mean, I’m here because this has been going on for almost a year, and I know it’s wearing me down.

But I can’t just say it’s unreasonable, because the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That’s the part everyone skips over. My family keeps saying, “You need to let this go,” and the doctors say the numbers are fine, but they weren’t the same—something in the clinic system is changing it or holding parts back, and if I stop checking, then what? Then it just gets buried.

And I know I go in circles with it. I’ll be doing something normal, like laundry or getting ready for work, and then I remember one date or one result and I have to go look again. So yes, it’s… it’s too much in the sense that I’m exhausted. But I don’t think the reason I’m checking is wrong.
Do thoughts about your dad’s lab results ever feel intrusive and unwanted, like they keep popping into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yeah… they do pop in, but I don’t know if “unwanted” is the right word. I don’t want to be thinking about it all the time, obviously. I’ll be trying to make dinner or driving somewhere and suddenly I’m back on that chart in my head, like the numbers, the dates, what was shown and what wasn’t.

It’s been almost a year of this. I’m here because I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and everyone—doctors, my family—keeps telling me the numbers are fine. But the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

So yes, it comes into my mind even when I’m trying to focus on something else. But it’s not random, you know? It’s because something is wrong there, and I can’t just pretend I didn’t see it.
Has there ever been a moment when you fully believed you might be wrong about the clinic changing or withholding your dad’s lab results?

Fully believed I might be wrong? No… not fully. I’ve had moments where I’m tired enough that I think, okay, maybe I missed something, maybe I’m not explaining it right. Like when my family keeps saying the numbers are fine, or the doctors say there’s nothing there, I try to sit with that for a second.

But then I go back to the chart, and it still doesn’t match what I saw. And I know how lab records are supposed to look—I mean, I’ve worked around this stuff, I’m not just making up numbers out of thin air. Sorry, that’s probably not what you asked exactly. It’s just… this has been almost a year of me trying to prove someone in that clinic system is changing something or holding parts of my dad’s results back, and everyone keeps acting like if they say “it’s fine” enough times, I’ll stop noticing.

So I can doubt myself for a minute, maybe. But fully believe I’m wrong? No. Not when the chart doesn’t line up.
Outside of this issue with your dad’s lab results, have you had times when your thoughts felt jumbled or people had trouble following what you were saying?

I don’t… I don’t think so? I mean, people have told me I go on too long sometimes, but that’s usually because they’re not listening to the part that matters.

Outside of my dad’s records, I guess I can get sidetracked. Like at work, if someone asks me something simple, I might explain the whole background because otherwise people misunderstand things, and then suddenly they’re looking at me like I’m making it complicated. But jumbled? I don’t know. That sounds like I’m not making sense, and I don’t think that’s what’s happening.

Sometimes I probably talk around the point. I’m doing it now, probably. But I haven’t really noticed people not being able to follow me unless they already don’t want to hear what I’m saying.
When this started, were you going through a period of feeling unusually depressed?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I mean, I was upset, definitely, but it was more because things weren’t lining up and nobody seemed to want to look at it the way I was seeing it.

When you say “unusually depressed,” do you mean like sad for no reason, or not functioning? Because I don’t really know how to separate that from being stressed when something serious is happening. I remember being preoccupied with it, and frustrated, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as depression.
Over the past year, have you become much less interested in seeing people or doing your usual activities?

I don’t know if I’d say “much less interested.” I mean, I still see people when I need to, and I still do things, but it’s harder when every conversation turns into someone telling me to “let it go,” like that’s helpful.

So maybe I’ve pulled back some, but not because I suddenly don’t care about people or activities. It’s more like… if I go to dinner with my sister and she brings up how I’m “stuck on this,” then the whole night changes, and I’m sitting there thinking about what she doesn’t understand. And then I’d rather just stay home and look over things myself, because at least that feels like I’m doing something.

But usual activities… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really been keeping track that way.
Have you ever filed a formal complaint or contacted authorities because you believed the clinic was altering your dad’s lab results?

I mean… I’ve thought about it. That’s part of why I’m here, honestly, because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding parts of my dad’s lab results back.

It’s not like I woke up one day and decided to make trouble. I know what I saw in the chart, and then later it didn’t match, and everybody keeps saying, “The numbers are fine,” or “You’re reading too much into it,” but that’s not the same as explaining why it changed.

So… formal complaint, authorities—I don’t know if I’ve done it the way you mean. But I’ve been trying to get someone to take it seriously, because it’s wearing me down.
Has this belief about your dad’s lab results ever led you to think you were receiving special messages or hidden signs meant specifically for you?

Special messages? I don’t know… not like a TV talking to me or anything like that, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more that the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That’s why I’m here. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And everyone keeps saying the numbers are fine—doctors, my family, everybody—but that doesn’t explain why it was one way and then later it wasn’t.

I mean, when you work around labs, you notice details. I’m a phlebotomist, so I know people miss things, or they act like you don’t understand because you’re “too close” to it. My aunt does that too, she’ll say, “Just listen to the doctor,” like that ends the conversation. But it doesn’t.

So… hidden signs meant for me, no, I don’t think of it like that. It’s the records. The mismatch. That’s what I keep coming back to, and it’s been wearing me down.
Do you believe it is actually possible for someone in the clinic system to alter or withhold your dad’s lab results without others noticing?

Yes, I do think it’s possible. I mean, people act like systems are perfect just because they’re “systems,” but I work around labs, and I know how things can get entered, reviewed, released, changed—there are steps where something could be held back or made to look normal.

And I’m not saying every single person there would have to know. That’s what my sister keeps saying, like, “You think everyone’s in on it?” No, that’s not what I’m saying. It could be one person, or a small part of the process, and everyone else just repeats what’s in the chart because that’s what they see.

That’s why I’m here. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors and my family keep telling me the numbers are fine, but I know what I saw before, and the chart doesn’t match now. It’s exhausting. It’s like I’m the only one willing to look at the actual mismatch.
Do you think the idea that the clinic is changing your dad’s lab results could be coming from your own mind, rather than actually happening?

I mean… I know why you’re asking that, but no, I don’t think it’s just coming from my mind. That’s what everyone keeps trying to make it sound like, like because I’m stressed or because it’s my dad, I must be seeing things wrong.

But I know what I saw in the chart. And then later it didn’t match. I work around lab stuff, so I notice when something is off—maybe not everything, but enough to know when numbers or entries don’t line up.

It’s just… for the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding back parts of his lab results, and doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine. My aunt says I’m making myself sick over it, which—maybe I am wearing myself down, but that doesn’t mean the mismatch isn’t real.

So, could stress make me focus on it more? Maybe. But the idea itself isn’t just in my head. The chart changed. That’s the part nobody wants to answer.
Because of this belief about your dad’s lab results, have you had trouble keeping up with your work?

Not really with the actual work, no. I mean, I think about it a lot, and sometimes it follows me around in my head, but I still show up for my phlebotomy shifts. I do my draws, I handle the patients, I keep to the schedule.

It’s funny because people act like if you’re upset about one thing, suddenly you can’t function at all, but that’s not true. Like, I still pay my bills, I still get groceries, I still keep myself together. I have my routine. I know where everything is in my apartment, I do laundry on Sundays usually—unless I’m covering a shift, which happens more than people think.

So, no, I haven’t lost my job or stopped going in or anything like that. It’s mostly this thing with my dad’s records that takes up space. Outside of that, I’m managing day to day.
Has anyone else ever actually seen the lab result you believe was changed, besides you?

I mean, not the exact one the way I saw it, no. That’s part of the problem, right? Because by the time I tried to point it out, everyone was looking at the later version in the chart and saying, “See, it’s fine.” But that isn’t what I saw before.

And I know that sounds convenient, like I’m the only one who saw it, but I work around this stuff. I know how a result can be there and then later the record looks different, or something is missing, and everyone just trusts what’s currently in front of them.

I’ve been trying for a year to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. My family keeps acting like I’m obsessing, and the doctors just repeat that the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It’s wearing me down because nobody else caught it before it changed.
Outside of your dad’s lab results, have you often believed you could sense connections or meanings that other people would say are unusual?

I’m not sure what you mean by “connections or meanings.” Like, do you mean signs? Because people use that word and then suddenly it sounds like you’re saying I think everything is a message, and I don’t… I don’t walk around thinking billboards are talking to me or anything.

I mean, I notice patterns at work sometimes, but that’s normal in a lab setting. You get used to numbers, times, initials, little changes in how things are entered. My coworker jokes that I can spot a mislabeled tube from across the room, which isn’t magic, it’s just paying attention. And honestly, some people don’t pay attention, they just click through whatever is on the screen.

But outside my dad’s results? I don’t know. I can’t think of anything like that. I’m mostly focused on what happened with his chart. That’s the part that matters.
Do you ever feel that your belief that the clinic changed your dad’s lab results is irrational or doesn’t make sense?

No. I mean… I know other people think it doesn’t make sense, because they keep saying the numbers are fine and acting like I’m making some huge leap. But to me it’s the opposite. The chart doesn’t match what I saw.

That’s why I’ve been trying for the past year to prove someone in the clinic system changed something or held part of it back. And it’s not like I woke up one day and decided this for no reason. I work around lab stuff, I know how records are supposed to look. My dad’s chart was different.

I guess I get tired and I think, why can’t anyone else see this? But that doesn’t make it irrational. It just means they’re looking at what’s there now, not what was there before.
